chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammara ibn Khallad, who said: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying:
"Three [things] are from the Sunnah of the Messengers: using perfume, trimming the hair, and frequenting the paths (socializing/moving about)."
ai.seo_question: What are the three Sunnah practices of the Prophets mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) identifies these three practices as Sunan al-Mursalun, linking personal hygiene and social engagement to the prophetic tradition of balancing spiritual devotion with worldly presence. The term 'kathrat al-tarouqah' specifically emphasizes active participation in community life, countering ascetic isolationism often found in other traditions. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on 'Tayyibat' (purity and goodness) in both physical appearance and social conduct as acts of worship.
